claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Oilers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. Hot take: the Kings shut it down.
claims.call: The Kings keep the Oilers’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).

claims.head: The Oilers’ power play is a weapon
claims.body: On the power play, Edmonton is the league’s best, but Los Angeles is near the bottom. Every penalty the Kings take could cost them. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

notes.text: Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 57% of the team’s power-play time in 5 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 30% last season.

LAK.head: A slightly uphill night for the Kings
LAK.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Los Angeles has home-ice advantage. The Kings can tip it if they keep dangerous shots away.

EDM.head: The Oilers start a half-step ahead
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Los Angeles has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Kings can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Kings are still looking for their first win
paras: The Kings are still looking for their first win of the season, 0-2-2 through four games. The Oilers have won four straight.

It’s strength against strength: the Oilers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. The Oil’s power play bites, but the Kings’ doesn’t.

items.text: Mathieu Joseph faces his old team, Los Angeles.
The Oilers are newly without Frederik Andersen, and have had to make do without Zach Hyman, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Matt Savoie all season. Devon Levi is expected to start.
Leon Draisaitl has a point in six straight games against Los Angeles, and 14 points in his last eight against them.
Connor McDavid is set to play his 800th NHL game.
